<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/platform-objects/src/pages/sys-organization.page.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **143** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json bfc1539fe00a33bc3215614a8d6c76a05eb8e8aa` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `bb1389f0b5efb952c5f320e0e438791bab652344` — the merge of head `473c6ff949110fbc6f4c5e12ee3116cc895128a1` into base `bfc1539fe00a33bc3215614a8d6c76a05eb8e8aa`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin bb1389f0b5efb952c5f320e0e438791bab652344 && git checkout bb1389f0b5efb952c5f320e0e438791bab652344
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin bfc1539fe00a33bc3215614a8d6c76a05eb8e8aa 473c6ff949110fbc6f4c5e12ee3116cc895128a1 && git checkout -B drift-repro bfc1539fe00a33bc3215614a8d6c76a05eb8e8aa && git merge --no-ff 473c6ff949110fbc6f4c5e12ee3116cc895128a1

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json bfc1539fe00a33bc3215614a8d6c76a05eb8e8aa
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs bfc1539fe00a33bc3215614a8d6c76a05eb8e8aa` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

### ① Derived judgments

**The removal — right.** The diff's three hunks in `sys-organization.object.ts` are a comment on `leave_organization` (202–210), a comment on `rename_organization` (226–240) and the `change_slug` block (255–290); nothing else in the file moves, so `create_organization`, `update_organization`, `delete_organization`, `set_active_organization`, `invite_user`, `leave_organization` and `rename_organization` are byte-identical in declaration, declared order and gate. Every remaining `type: 'api'` target is under `/api/v1/auth/organization/`, a better-auth door the open-source composition mounts; the only `/api/v1/cloud/` target left the object. On an open-source multi-org composition the record page therefore offers no action whose target answers `404`. The object's comments are true under the console's order model (objectui `containers.tsx`: `order` ascending with unset read as 0, `variant: 'primary'` tie-break, then stable registration order; the record header is `invite_user` at order -1, `set_active_organization` 0, `rename_organization` 0, `leave_organization` 1; `maxVisible` 3 puts leave alone in the overflow's destructive band). The page docblock now says the same and is true.

**The cloud-shaped binding — right, with one unstated qualifier.** `attachBoundActions` runs in `finishServedObject`, the tail of every object read (`resolveObject`, the code layer, the stored-row and MetadataService folds), and attaches by reference every standalone `action` a code package ships whose `standaloneActionOwnerKey` is the object's name and whose package is not disabled, deduplicated by name, after the object's own actions, the attached ones stable-sorted by `order` among themselves. A top-level action is parsed by the same `ActionSchema` whose transform lowers `requiresFeature` to `visible` (`lowerRequiresFeature(lowerRequiresMembershipReach(data))`, `features.*` last), so the served `visible` is `features.multiOrgEnabled != false`, identical to `leave_organization`'s, with no `gatedInputs` row consulted. Target, method, location and the one `slug` param travel by reference. Header position under the console's sort: invite (-1), set_active (0), rename (0), change_slug (0, registered after the object's own actions), leave (1); so change_slug sits in the overflow, in the non-destructive band ahead of leave, exactly where the platform copy sat. The pin's fixture is the removed declaration's fourteen keys and values unchanged plus `objectName`, which `sameActionDeclaration` excludes as a provenance key: a faithful copy. Qualifier the PR body does not carry: this is the synthesized header. Cloud's own organization page lists its header actions explicitly (`actions: ['leave_organization', 'change_slug']`, per #24271's body), and a `page:header` resolves ids against its own object's served actions (ruling 6228318638, B′ on #24034), which now carry the attached action; on cloud the position is the page list's, not `order`'s, and the resolution is unmeasured there.

**The transition — right.** While cloud's pin still carries the platform copy: `attachBoundActions` skips the name (`present.has`), so the platform copy is served; `FIND_BOUND_ACTION_COLLISIONS` skips a pair that `sameActionDeclaration` holds equal (structural equality minus `_`-stamps, `protection`, `objectName`), so an identical cloud declaration is served once with no report; a differing one is reported at `kernel:ready` by `reportBoundActionCollisions` as one `warn` per pair naming the object, the action and both packages, the boot goes on, and the object keeps serving its own (#24472's rung 1, the maintainer's "18.x, report first", 6262054499). A `type: 'api'` action registers no handler, so the handler-face warning does not fire for this pair. The PR body's section 3 and the platform-objects changeset's Fix line tell cloud exactly this.

**`gatedInputs` — right.** Readers of the rows on the head: `feature-gate-guard.test.ts` (walks `identity`, `metadata`, `system` of `packages/platform-objects` only) and `public-auth-features.test.ts` (grammar and the gates-XOR-exempt rule). `featureGatePredicate` and `lowerRequiresFeature` read `semantics`; plugin-auth's `public-feature-registry.test.ts` reads the key set and `semantics`; `requiresFeature` is `z.enum(PUBLIC_AUTH_FEATURE_NAMES)`, keys not rows; no `packages/lint` rule, runtime path or gate reads `gatedInputs` to admit or refuse any action. The row is the platform objects' own census. The guard keeps teeth: forward is `it.each` over the 38 remaining rows (39 on the base), reverse is `it.each` over every `features.*` reference with a floor of 37 (38 references on the head); restoring only the platform copy reds reverse (an unbooked `features.multiOrgEnabled` reference), restoring only the row reds forward (no such action), which is the dev's ablation reading.

**The translations — right.** Each of the four bundles loses exactly the `change_slug` subtree (`label`, `description`, `successMessage`, five lines) at the same position; no other key moves. The generator (`os i18n extract` over `scripts/i18n-extract.config.ts`, the committed bundle as merge baseline, `--fill=default --source-hashes`) emits only the keys the schema walk yields, so a removed action's subtree leaves every locale, `en` included, and no `source-hashes` companion carried `change_slug` on the base. The mechanical proof is on the head: `pnpm check:i18n` (self-test plus `check-i18n-bundles.mjs`, verdict 1 = bundle drift) runs in lint.yml's `typecheck-consumers` under `continue-on-error`, whose outcome the lane-end `OS_LANE_STEPS` reader at lint.yml:6612 re-reads; that check-run, `Type Check · consumer gates`, is `success`.

**The pins — right, with one bare deletion and one CI gap.** `sys-organization-rename-action.test.ts` asserts the exact header order, the sorted seven-name api set with every target matching `^/api/v1/auth/organization/[a-z-]+$`, and `change_slug` absent. `platform-objects.test.ts` adds a completeness pin: the set of actions whose `visible.source` names `features.multiOrgEnabled` equals the matrix's `SysOrganization` rows. `confirm-question-carryover.test.ts` pins 13 pairs and `change_slug` absent from all five bundles with `rename_organization` as the control. `action-execution-destructive.test.ts` pins the flipped set at 5, the full set at 13 and `change_slug` absent. `org-record-admin-reach` drops the `UNDECIDED` hold-out, pins the served set equal to the seven graded actions and probes every api action the record serves. Judged from the code, with the platform copy restored that file reds in two cases: the served set gains `change_slug` (strict `toEqual`), and the probe POSTs `/cloud/organizations/org_does_not_exist/change-slug`, the router answers `404`, and both the `status === 404` filter and the name-set equality fail; the dev's "red 2" reading holds. `org-change-slug-bound-action` asserts served once, target, method, location, param, `visible` equal to `featureGatePredicate('multiOrgEnabled')` and to leave's, admitted/hidden under `celEngine`, the header order with change_slug between rename and leave, and no `WARN`/`ERROR` line naming `'change_slug'`; under the ablation it stays green by construction, as reported. `action-confirm-one-dialog.test.ts` is the one bare deletion (the map loses its row, no new assertion); the absence is pinned in four other files, so it is acceptable. Pin-quality note, not a verdict ground: the new file's "no collision" case first asserts that some `WARN` line was captured at all, so it depends on an unrelated boot warning being present. CI gap: see ③.

### ② Semver level

- **Packages and levels — right.** `@objectstack/platform-objects: minor` and `@objectstack/spec: minor`. Both are breaking narrowings; under the launch-window convention (`check-changeset-no-major.mjs:58`, `:1670`: a `(narrowing)` is BREAKING and ships `minor`) and with the RC exemption not active (see the next item) a `major` would be refused, so `minor` is the enforced grade. `Check Changeset` (pr-automation.yml: `check-empty-changeset`, `check-adr-0087-registration`, `check-changeset-no-major`, each with `--self-test`) is `success` on the head.
- **BREAKING banner — present in both, FROM / TO / Fix each on its own bullet; the counts are right** (seven `sys_organization` rows to six; the eight served actions to seven). **`Clause-②: no (narrowing) (...)` opens a line in both changesets and in the PR body.** `readClause2Line` reads value `no` and arm `narrowing`: `matchValueToken` stops at `no` before a non-word character, `readArmToken` matches `(narrowing` and reads nothing after it, so the trailing parenthetical is ignored; `no (narrowing)` is not the refused `no (widening)` contradiction.
- **ADR-0087 — right.** Exactly one `adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription) ...` marker per changeset; `readDisposition` parses category `no-migration-prescription` with the rest as the why; the gate is green, so the FROM / TO / Fix bullets were not read as a migration prescription. The category is the honest one: no authorable key, export or stored shape moves and nothing is rewritten; the repair is another composition's declaration.
- **Widening — none.** No new export, public member or accepted key: the engine (`FIND_BOUND_ACTION_COLLISIONS`, `attachBoundActions`) is untouched, the test files add no surface, `PUBLIC_AUTH_FEATURES` keeps its keys and entry type. **The spec removal is a narrowing a consumer can feel**: the constant is `as const`, so `typeof PUBLIC_AUTH_FEATURES.multiOrgEnabled.gatedInputs` loses a literal member and the runtime array loses a string; the spec changeset says both. No generated artifact mirrors the census (the row's siblings appear only in the source file), so `check:generated` and the api-surface baselines are unaffected, consistent with `Spec property liveness` and the lint lanes green.
- **One false statement in a changeset body — the ground of the verdict.** `.changeset/24318-platform-objects-change-slug-to-cloud.md` line 13 says the change ships as `minor` "under the launch-window convention for breaking changes (`.changeset/pre.json` is open in `next` pre mode)". On this head `.changeset/pre.json` is `{"mode": "exit", "tag": "next"}` (origin/main `c46b5f14cf`, "exit Changesets pre mode (`next`), so the next version pass cuts the 18.0.0 GA", #24555): pre mode is not open. The sentence also has the mechanism backwards: `check-changeset-no-major.mjs:105–110` names the pre-mode state as the RC EXEMPTION under which a `major` is admitted; it is the exited state, this head's, under which the launch-window guard is armed and a breaking change ships `minor`. `changeset version` compiles this paragraph into `packages/platform-objects/CHANGELOG.md`, which AGENTS.md marks RELEASE-OWNED: a factual error in a released entry is amended only in a dedicated docs-only PR and never in a code PR. The spec changeset's parallel sentence carries no pre-mode claim and is right. Fix before the queue: delete the parenthetical, or replace it with "pre mode exited at `c46b5f14cf`; the launch-window convention ships a breaking change as `minor`". One line, no code, no re-measurement.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **`sys-organization.page.ts` outside the claim's `File surface` — accepted.** The fold-in note 6249926047 named this docblock for this card's touch, the first claim 6254536343 listed the file, and the removal made the sentence false; two lines, comment only, true now.
- **Spec and runtime full suites on the pre-merge head `048de3158` — accepted.** The merge `91dc52d3e` brought four `main` commits, none touching the diff's files; on the head, `Test Core` shards 1–6 are `success` and the aggregate is `queued` at this read, so the check-runs answer this family for the head once the aggregate settles.
- **Changesets carrying the claim's whole `Clause-②` line with its parenthetical — accepted.** Read as `declared / no / narrowing` by the single reader (`clause2-line.mjs`), identical on the PR body and both changesets, and `Check Changeset` is green.
- **The new dogfood pin green under the ablation by construction — accepted.** An identical platform copy serves the same bytes and `sameActionDeclaration` holds; the ablation target is `org-record-admin-reach`, which reds in two cases by the code above, and the PR body says so.
- **Added: the dogfood family has no CI verdict on this head.** ci.yml's two speeds (#22998): the `dogfood` shards carry `github.event_name != 'pull_request' && github.event_name != 'merge_group'`, so they skipped here (`Dogfood Regression Gate (matrix.shard/3): skipped`), and `dogfood-gate` (`Dogfood Regression Gate: success`) keeps `if: always()` and concludes success on zero expected attestations. Neither this PR's run nor the merge group runs the moved pin or the new one; their first CI measurement is `main`'s hourly full battery after landing, read by the publish lane. The dev's local 12/12 is the only run, read as a claim; both files are judged right from the code above. The seat accepts that claim or asks the dev for the two-file dogfood run on the head; this record did not probe.
- **Added: a bare deletion and a brittle sanity check** (①, the pins): `action-confirm-one-dialog.test.ts` loses a row with no new assertion, covered elsewhere; the new pin's `bootLines.some(WARN)` precondition rests on an unrelated warning.
- **Open question 1 (header position of cloud's copy): A.** By the four axes: business need, cloud wants Change Slug where it was, and A gives that under the synthesized header; long-term soundness, A is the only shape that is `sameActionDeclaration`-equal to the platform copy, so B's explicit `order` would be a DIFFERING declaration on every cloud boot until the pin bump, one `warn` naming `com.objectstack.plugin-auth` each boot with the platform copy served under its own order anyway; AI safety, one copied declaration is the hardest to get wrong; startup scope, no new requirement. And on cloud's page the header is an explicit `actions` list (#24271), so B buys nothing there either. The dev's recommendation stands, with the stronger reason it did not give.
- **Open question 2 (does cloud's bundle reach `sys_organization._actions`): A.** The in-memory i18n service deep-merges every `loadTranslations(locale, data)` into one tree per locale (`memory-i18n.ts:182–189`), platform plugins push theirs at `kernel:ready`, and `resolveKey` walks `objects.sys_organization._actions.change_slug.label` whichever package pushed it; the console reads the key through the shared localizer with the authored literal as fallback (`containers.tsx`, `resolveLabel`), so a miss degrades to the English declaration, never to a broken button. The cloud seat measures on cloud's boot; a card (class a) only on a measured miss. B is premature.
- **Cross-lane surface — what the seat declares before the queue.** To `domain:spec`: `packages/spec/src/kernel/public-auth-features.ts`, one row leaving the published `as const` census, `@objectstack/spec: minor`, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, no key, enum value, export or generated artifact moves, the platform objects' guard the only reader.
